method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the writing-l4-rules skill; the s 147 duty with a deadline is a regulative rule (PARTY ... MUST ... WITHIN ... LEST BREACH ... BECAUSE) run inside a plain-fact question; no REFUSE (gaps answer NOTHING or a named constructor, asserted); every judgment of the court asked as an input; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. A new layer beside baseline-2026-10 and naive-2026-10, which are untouched. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Competition and Consumer Act 2010, Compilation No. 166, compilation date 2026-08-27 (includes amendments up to Act No. 76, 2026), register id C2026C00389, deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/C2004A00109.txt, with the s 87M and s 87Z formulas from C2004A00109.formulas.md. Competition and Consumer Regulations 2010, Compilation No. 100 (register id F2026C00856), searched: no rate or figure for Part VIB is prescribed, so the Act's defaults apply. CPI, average weekly earnings, the bond rate and the superannuation charge percentage are inputs.

focus: the provisions a claimant meets: ACL Part 3-5 manufacturer liability, s 236 damages (with s 237), and Part VIB personal injury damages limits
scope: From the claimant's seat: Schedule 2 (Australian Consumer Law) ss 7, 9 (as an input), 138-144, 146-150, 236, 237(1)-(3); the Act's ss 137A, 137B, 137C, 137E; Part VIB ss 87D, 87E, 87F-87K, 87L-87S, 87U, 87W, 87X, 87Y, 87Z, 87ZA, 87ZB, 87ZC(1). Out: ACL s 18 and the consumer guarantees (in baseline-2026-10); ss 138(3), 145 (State law); Part 5-4 Division 2; ss 238-243; the Act's ss 137D, 137F-137H; Part VIA; ss 87F(2), 87N, 87T, 87V (inputs or procedure), 87ZC(2)-(3); machinery.
seat: the claimant (the individual injured by goods with a safety defect, or the person who suffers loss through another's injury or death or through damage to household goods or a home; the person suing for loss caused by a contravention of Chapter 2 or 3 of the Australian Consumer Law; in s 87G(6), the personal representative of a deceased claimant)
